text: Deadlines are a part of professional life, but they don’t have to be stressful. The first step is good time management. Break a large project into smaller tasks and set mini-deadlines for each one. This makes the work feel less overwhelming. Next, learn to prioritize. Not everything is equally important, so focus on the most critical tasks first and be realistic about what you can achieve. Also, practice scope management: if a project keeps growing, don’t be afraid to say no or negotiate what is truly necessary. Finally, communicate early. If you see a problem, tell your team or client before it becomes a crisis. Clear communication can lead to adjusted timelines, and an honest update is always better than a late surprise.
